dedupe_keys.name: rcra subtitle d 258 seismic design guidance for municipal solid waste landfill facilities us epa epa 600 r 95 051 1995

description: This US EPA guidance explains how municipal solid waste landfills should be sited and designed to meet the earthquake rules of the federal RCRA Subtitle D regulations, 40 CFR Part 258, which took effect in October 1993. Prepared in 1995 by Richardson, Kavazanjian and Matasović for EPA's Risk Reduction Engineering Laboratory, it covers two requirements. The first bars new landfills or expansions within 200 feet of a fault active in the Holocene unless a smaller setback is shown to be safe, and the guidance describes field methods to identify such faults. The second requires landfills in seismic impact zones, where USGS maps give peak bedrock acceleration above 0.1 g, to be designed to resist regional earthquakes, and the guidance gives design procedures and sample analyses for liners, leachate collection and surface water controls. The 155-page document is free to download as a PDF from the Federal Remediation Technologies Roundtable library. Coverage is United States landfill regulation as of 1995. Caveats: the scanned PDF has limited text, the hazard maps it cites have since been replaced, and later research on geosynthetic interfaces is not reflected. Simulation uses: design thresholds and failure modes for representing landfill damage and containment loss in earthquake scenarios. Related records: EPA's Landfill Methane Outreach Program database (data-epa-lmop-landfill-and-project-database) lists US landfills that such an analysis could be applied to.

schema_summary: Design guidance: field identification of Holocene faults for the 200-foot setback of section 258.13; seismic impact zones of section 258.14 from USGS probability maps (peak bedrock acceleration above 0.1 g); design procedures and sample analyses for the waste containment system (liners, leachate collection, surface water control) under a range of site and facility conditions
